test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question:
The volume of a solid cylinder is 2002 cm³ and its height is 13 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of its base?

(Take π = {(22)/(7)})
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a cylinder is the product of its base area and its height.

Base Area = Volume ÷ Height

Base Area = 2002 ÷ 13 = 154 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of the solid cylinder (V) = 2002 cm³

Height of the cylinder (h) = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h = (Base Area) × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0fdcacaf0b40f0498428405eef42c9fb0cd78b4c924186f809b2e29631cca02.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = Base Area × Height

⇒ 2002 = Base Area × 13

⇒ Base Area = 2002 ÷ 13

⇒ Base Area = 154 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The capacity of a cylinder calculated as V = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface only, given by the formula CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the areas of the two circular bases and the curved surface: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Base Area

The area of the circular bottom (or top) of the cylinder: Base Area = πr².</p
